sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time 2026-11-02 17:37 UTC; daily view captured on 2026-11-02. Date range 2026-11-02 through 2026-11-02.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent infrastructure is the clearest signal today: T3 Code, Agent Desktop, and Claude-Mem lead the captured daily star-gain list, while local inference and specialist developer tools provide strong secondary currents.

sections.title: pingdotgg/t3code
sections.description: An open-source agent-harness control surface that lets users operate local coding agents through mobile, web, and desktop clients.
sections.why_notable: The strongest daily star-gain signal in the snapshot; its cross-client control surface sits at the intersection of agent tools and developer UX.
sections.unique_caveat: The README describes the project as very early-stage.

sections.title: vercel-labs/agent-desktop
sections.description: A Rust-based CLI and C library for agents to inspect and operate desktop apps through OS accessibility trees and stable element references.
sections.why_notable: Second-highest daily gain and a concrete alternative to screenshot-only computer use, with cross-platform CLI/C interfaces.
sections.unique_caveat: Desktop access requires OS/session permissions; snapshots and command output can expose private screen content.

sections.title: thedotmack/claude-mem
sections.description: Persistent context for coding agents: captures session work, compresses it, and injects relevant memories into later sessions.
sections.why_notable: Strong daily momentum around a practical bottleneck in agent workflows: carrying useful context across sessions.
sections.unique_caveat: The README presents Claude Code as its core use case even while advertising compatibility with other agents; check current integrations.

sections.title: Donchitos/Claude-Code-Game-Studios
sections.description: A Claude Code configuration that organizes game development as a coordinated AI studio with specialist agents, skills, hooks, and rules.
sections.why_notable: A high-gain example of domain-specific agent orchestration rather than a general-purpose coding assistant.
sections.unique_caveat: Trending text says 72 skills while the current README lists 74, indicating fast-changing counts.

sections.title: mattpocock/skills
sections.description: A set of small, composable engineering skills for coding agents, intended to be adaptable and usable across models.
sections.why_notable: Shows demand for reusable agent workflows and human-editable skills rather than monolithic process frameworks.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a skills collection, not a standalone agent or application.

sections.title: D4Vinci/Scrapling
sections.description: A Python web-scraping framework spanning single requests through full crawls, with adaptive parsing and browser-backed workflows.
sections.why_notable: A notable non-agent developer-tool signal with substantial daily gains, extending the snapshot beyond the agent wave.
sections.unique_caveat: Scraping behavior remains subject to target-site terms and access controls.

sections.title: shiyu-coder/Kronos
sections.description: A foundation model project for learning the language of financial markets, with pretrained models and evaluation materials.
sections.why_notable: A domain-specific ML project among the top daily gainers, showing investor attention to specialized time-series models.
sections.unique_caveat: The default branch was last pushed on 2026-04-13; today’s star gain is not evidence of a same-day code release.

sections.title: JustVugg/colibri
sections.description: A dependency-light C inference engine that streams mixture-of-experts model weights from disk to run large models on local hardware.
sections.why_notable: A fast-rising example of low-level, local inference engineering rather than hosted-model access.
sections.unique_caveat: Supported model families and practical performance depend on hardware and model-specific engines.

sections.title: FlashML-org/FreeToken
sections.description: An edge-native MoE serving engine that combines GPU, CPU, memory, and interconnect resources to run large open models locally.
sections.why_notable: Pairs with Colibri as a distinct approach to consumer-scale inference, emphasizing adaptive CPU–GPU serving and caching.
sections.unique_caveat: The README’s documented native GPU support centers on NVIDIA RTX 30/40/50 series; verify current device compatibility.

sections.title: hyprwm/Hyprland
sections.description: An independent, customizable dynamic tiling Wayland compositor focused on modern features and visual polish.
sections.why_notable: A mature Linux desktop project in the daily list provides a useful counterpoint to the agent-heavy cohort.
sections.unique_caveat: It targets Linux systems using Wayland.

sections.title: paperclipai/paperclip
sections.description: An open-source application for coordinating and managing AI agents at work.
sections.why_notable: Adds an organization/management layer to the agent trend, complementary to tools that execute coding tasks directly.

sections.title: kornia/kornia
sections.description: A Python geometric computer-vision library for spatial AI and differentiable vision workflows.
sections.why_notable: A long-running computer-vision library still drawing daily attention, offering a data/ML counterpoint to coding agents.

sections.title: deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype
sections.description: A proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged for DeepSeek Harness; it listens to GitHub and optionally Feishu, acts on authorized requests or team rules, and can return results such as pull requests.
sections.why_notable: A newly created repository (2026-10-31) surfaced in the corroborating GitHub Search query with 12,444 stars; it illustrates autonomous, event-triggered coding agents. It was not on the captured daily Trending page, so no comparable daily star gain is available.
sections.unique_caveat: The README explicitly labels it a research prototype, not an official DeepSeek product or production-ready system, and says it differs from the accompanying paper.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content:
- **Agent control planes and orchestration:** Several entries are moving beyond one-shot code generation toward running, routing, or coordinating agents: T3 Code exposes local agents across clients; Paperclip manages agents at work; the DeepSeek prototype reacts to authorized repository events; and Game Studios composes specialist roles. Agent Desktop supplies the computer-use interface layer.
- **Persistent context and reusable agent skills:** Claude-Mem addresses cross-session context, while mattpocock/skills packages small, composable engineering procedures. Both focus on making agent work repeatable across sessions rather than merely adding another model.
- **Local inference for large mixture-of-experts models:** FreeToken emphasizes edge-native CPU–GPU co-execution and caching; colibri streams expert weights from disk in a lightweight C runtime. The shared theme is using consumer hardware more efficiently, with distinct runtime designs.
- **Automation and developer infrastructure beyond agents:** Scrapling’s scraper framework stands out as a conventional developer-tool project with strong daily gain, showing the snapshot is not exclusively about AI agents.
- **Specialized ML and computer vision:** Kronos targets financial-market time series, while Kornia provides geometric computer-vision building blocks. These are narrower ML domains rather than general coding-agent infrastructure.
- **Linux desktop systems:** Hyprland remains a high-visibility Wayland compositor alongside the new agent-facing desktop automation represented by Agent Desktop; they address different layers of desktop use.
- **Languages:** 4 TypeScript, 4 Python, 2 Shell, and 1 each Rust, C, and C++; this is based on the 13 listed repositories, including one supplemental Search result.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: The strongest common thread is the move from isolated coding assistants to systems that control desktop surfaces, retain context, and coordinate multi-step work. At the same time, two very different local MoE runtimes and a strong scraping project show continued appetite for practical infrastructure. The DeepSeek prototype is a notable fresh Search discovery, but its README warns that it is research code and its stars cannot be compared directly with the daily Trending gains.

sections.title: Sources and Method
sections.content:
Primary source: https://github.com/trending?since=daily
Corroboration: GitHub REST API repository metadata and default-branch commit endpoints for listed repos; Search API query https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=created%3A2026-10-31..2026-11-02+stars%3A%3E50&sort=stars&order=desc&per_page=30 for the supplemental new-repository signal. README files were read for narration-priority repositories.
Method note: The 12 primary entries are sorted by the stars-today counts on the captured daily Trending view. The DeepSeek prototype is appended as a clearly marked Search-discovered supplement; GitHub does not provide a comparable daily Trending gain for it. Total stars and default-branch commit SHAs were corroborated via REST API. The Trending page is a live snapshot, not a guaranteed midnight-to-midnight event ledger.
